types.name: enhancement
types.description: A new feature, or a change to how something works

types.description: Asks how something works or whether something is possible

types.name: documentation

areas.area:tui: Terminal UI: rendering, the input box, keyboard handling, scrollback, layout, themes
areas.area:tools: Built-in tools, tool calling and validation, custom tools, git tools
areas.area:cli: CLI flags, headless and plain mode, `nanocoder run`, shell completions, slash commands
areas.area:providers: LLM providers, model configuration, the client factory, tokenisation, context limits
areas.area:agent: The agent loop: context management, compaction, subagents, memory, sessions, checkpoints, planning
areas.area:vscode: The VS Code extension and the ACP integration

flags.performance: Speed, memory use or token efficiency is the substance of the issue
flags.architecture: Requires a structural design change across modules
flags.good first issue: Small, well-specified and self-contained: a newcomer could fix it from the issue alone

proposalGuidance: A proposal is a speculative idea, a design exploration or an 'is there interest in…' post: something to discuss rather than something anyone has committed to build. Concrete, clearly scoped features — a new flag, a new slash command, a fix to how an existing feature behaves — are not proposals, however large.
scopeGuidance: Nanocoder is a local-first CLI coding agent. Out of scope: requests to bundle or endorse a specific commercial product or service, features that require a hosted Nano Collective backend, and support for models or providers through anything other than a standard API. Integrations reachable through MCP or a custom provider configuration are in scope as documentation, not as built-in code.
